o: Among the even values in `nums`, return the one appearing most often; break ties by smaller value; return -1 if there are no even numbers. In `[0,1,2,2,4,4,1]` the evens 2 and 4 both appear twice, so we return 2. In `[29,47,...]` there are no evens, so -1. With n ≤ 2000 even an O(n²) scan works, but a hash-map count gives O(n) cleanly.
k: Filter to even values, count with a hash map, then select by (max frequency, min value).

a.i: One pass builds a frequency map of even numbers; a second pass over the (at most n) distinct keys picks the entry with the highest count, breaking ties by smallest key.
s: Build a Counter of even elements.
Among keys achieving it, return the minimum; if the map is empty return -1.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to count, one pass over distinct keys

a.i: Sort a filtered list of even numbers; equal values become contiguous runs, so a single scan tracks the current run length and updates the answer whenever a longer run starts or an equally long run begins at a smaller value (automatic since the array is ascending).
s: Collect even numbers and sort them.
Scan runs of equal values, tracking best (length, value).
Return the best value or -1 if no evens exist.

w: Prefer the hash-map solution for its linear time. Watch for the empty-even case returning -1 and remember 0 is even. Tie-breaking by smallest value is the only subtle part; sorting handles it implicitly, the map version needs the explicit comparison.
